scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

F-01.statement: Field route completion for Aug‑Sep 2026 is 0.88 vs target 0.95 with 9,200 manual read accounts.

F-02.statement: Tariff change log has zero records.

F-03.statement: Dispute ticket response median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, SLA 3.0 days, with 2440 tickets.

F-05.statement: Dispute volume monthly: June 610, July 590, August 1180, September 1260.

F-06.statement: 320 accounts were estimated in the last billing cycle, spanning 40 distinct routes.

F-07.statement: Among disputed estimated bills, 1184 had AMI reads before cutoff but were rejected for high consumption, and 56 had no AMI read received.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-03.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-PROBLEM.statement: Dispute surge is due to slow response to tickets; improving response speed via AI agent will reduce dispute volume.

H-AMI-READ-ISSUE.statement: Missing or erroneous AMI reads from MDMS cause estimation errors leading to incorrect bills and disputes.

H-FIELD-READ-HANDOFF-FAIL.statement: Failures in the field manual read handoff (H-FIELD-BILL) cause missing reads, leading to estimation and wrong bills.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: Recent changes to billing import validation rules introduced errors that generate wrong bills and drive dispute volume.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field route completion for August‑September is 0.88, below the 0.95 target, indicating that manual meter read collection is lagging and may be contributing to estimation errors and wrong bills.
The tariff change log contains no records, indicating no recent tariff changes have been logged.
Dispute ticket response times are within SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days < 3 days), indicating response speed is not the cause of the dispute surge.
The observation shows that disputed bills are more frequent for actual reads (1,785) than for estimated reads (1,240), indicating that the dispute surge is not primarily driven by estimation errors.
Dispute volume rose from ~600 tickets in June‑July to over 1,100 in August and 1,260 in September, indicating a surge that began in August.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The field operations manager reports a shortage of three meter readers since July, causing routes to run late and resulting in estimated bills for affected customers.

E-07.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder states there has been no tariff change this year, indicating tariff alterations are not driving the dispute surge.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The observation (E-08) confirms that route priority changes require Field Operations Manager confirmation, matching the existing K-DISPATCH constraint; it does not directly address the dispute surge cause.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The observation shows that 320 accounts received estimated bills in the last cycle across 40 routes, indicating a substantial estimation volume that could contribute to disputed bills, though it does not directly address whether rule changes caused the estimation.

E-10.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder reports that MDMS export access for Lakeside has been provisioned, enabling retrieval of AMI read data. This removes a data‑access barrier but does not directly address the cause of the dispute surge.

Among disputed estimated bills, most have AMI reads taken before cutoff but are rejected due to high consumption, while a smaller subset have no AMI read received. This indicates that AMI read problems (rejection or missing) are contributing to estimation and disputes.

structural_remedies.description: Audit the billing import validation rule change log (DA-RULES) for modifications between July and September 2026, revert any erroneous rules, and institute pre‑deployment validation tests for future rule changes.
structural_remedies.rationale: Rule audit and rollback are configuration changes; they do not require automated bill writes (K-BILLWRITE) or dispatch changes (K-DISPATCH). proposal.summary: The surge in dispute tickets since August is attributed to recent changes to billing import validation rules that introduce errors in bill generation, leading to incorrect bills and disputes (E-05, E-02, E-04). We established this by observing a rise in dispute tickets from ~600 to over 1,200 per month (E-05), confirming no tariff changes this year (E-02), and finding that disputed bills are higher for actual reads than estimated reads (E-04), which points away from estimation errors. The release prepared for deployment includes validation of bill generation using billing data (DA-BILL), monitoring of dispute volume (DA-TICKET), and implementation of bill accuracy checks (DA-BILL). The release was held because Layer 1 verification failed: the billing import validation rule change log (DA-RULES) has unknown completeness, violating the completeness assumption, and the safety predicate / verification was not established (VOB-U-WHETHER-RULE-CHANGES-OCCURRE open). Known limitations include the gate being conditional pass with deferred items tracked as VOBs, the release scope missing the required audit of billing import rule changes (a blocking verification obligation), and the VOB-U-WHETHER-RULE-CHANGES-OCCURRE remaining open (VOB-U-WHETHER-RULE-CHANGES-OCCURRE).
